brief: Fed Governor Waller said on October 8 that he likely expects two additional rate hikes to be appropriate, which would raise the funds rate to 4.25-4.50%. Timing is flexible and hikes need not come at consecutive meetings. He said a strengthened labor market and persistent inflationary pressure, plus the unresolved Middle East conflict, AI-driven high-tech price increases, and tariff risk, have undermined his confidence that inflation is progressing to 2%. Core inflation is not showing sufficient progress. He cited the September dot plot, where eight participants see rates 50 basis points higher by end-2027, which markets read as 50 basis points of additional hikes ahead, and gave an example of three total 25bp hikes. He endorsed the Fed's dot-plot communication approach, implying he would oppose scrapping it. Goldman Sachs still expects one more 25bp hike in December, to 4-4.25%, but lowered its odds the FOMC skips December, since Waller's speech was a hawkish shift from his prior focus on three-month annualized core PCE, now 2.0%, consistent with Williams and Jefferson signaling an October skip. GS expects inflation data to improve enough by March to convince most of the FOMC that additional hikes are unnecessary.
